note: Monday pre-Asia-open sweep, 14 Sep 2026 07:02 SGT -- before SGX (09:00) and HKEX (09:30) open, after Friday 11 Sep's US close. Two corrections to Sunday's file: the Iran-Oman Muscat 'safe corridor' signing was POSTPONED late Saturday (it was never actually a Monday-signing story), and the Senate CLARITY Act cloture vote is confirmed TUESDAY 15 Sep, not Monday as previously mislabeled (15 Sep 2026 is a Tuesday). No SGX/HK-specific weekend news or fresh China rare-earth policy statement emerged beyond what's below; those threads carry the freshest confirmed reads.

items.headline: Oman postpones the Iran-Gulf Hormuz 'safe corridor' signing meeting slated for Monday
items.summary: Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi announced late Saturday (10:32pm local) that Monday's Muscat meeting to formalize an Iran-Oman Hormuz shipping corridor has been postponed 'in the interests of consensus.' A senior Iranian official had already told Reuters no signed deal was expected anyway, since Iran wants transit-fee rights that Oman rejects; Bahrain had separately confirmed it would boycott the wider Gulf talks. Iran has not struck any Gulf host state for a 4th straight day even as the diplomatic track stalls.
items.actionable: The near-term de-escalation catalyst markets may have been pricing for today just slipped -- Sunday's oil pop (Brent +2.8%, WTI +2.3%) likely persists into Monday's Asia/electronic open rather than fading, though the 4-day lull in Iranian strikes is a genuine counter-signal worth watching.

items.headline: FOMC meets Tue-Wed 15-16 Sep; a 25bp hike is the base case at ~85-90% priced, Fed in blackout until Thursday
items.summary: The Fed's next decision lands Wednesday 2pm ET off a current 3.5%-3.75% target range. CME-implied odds of a quarter-point hike jumped to roughly 85-90% after August's hotter-than-expected core CPI and held firm through the weekend. Fed officials are in a formal communications blackout from 5 Sep through 17 Sep, so no incremental Fed signal exists before the decision itself.
items.actionable: This remains the single biggest scheduled catalyst for the whole book this week -- the real surprise risk is a hold, which would likely spark an outsized relief rally in miners and S-REITs given how heavily a hike is already priced.

items.headline: Senate CLARITY Act cloture vote confirmed Tuesday 15 Sep, 2:15pm ET -- passage odds near 10-16%
items.summary: Multiple sources confirm the crypto market-structure bill's motion-to-proceed cloture vote is scheduled Tuesday, needing 60 votes (53 Republicans plus at least 7 Democrats). Three unresolved fights remain: ethics rules on Trump's roughly $1.4B personal crypto income, DeFi-developer liability, and a stablecoin-yield provision threatening about $1.35B of Coinbase USDC revenue. Passage odds on prediction markets have fallen from 82% in February to 10-16% now.
items.actionable: The vote lands Tuesday afternoon US time (Wednesday pre-dawn SGT), the same 24-hour window as the FOMC decision -- failure is largely priced in already, so the asymmetric surprise is to the upside if it somehow clears 60 votes.

items.headline: Bitcoin ETF weekly outflows hit $462.6M but slow sharply to $13.3M Friday as Ethereum ETFs take in $216M
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs logged $462.6M in net outflows for the week (worst single day -$282.6M on 10 Sep), before the daily pace slowed to just -$13.3M on Friday. Spot Ethereum ETFs moved the opposite way, taking in $216M that same Friday -- the sharpest BTC-to-ETH rotation of the year rather than a broad crypto exodus.
items.actionable: Read this as institutional money rotating within crypto, not exiting it outright -- worth tracking whether the rotation continues into Tuesday's CLARITY Act vote.

items.headline: China's rare-earth export halt to the US and Japan deepens ahead of the Sep 24 Trump-Xi summit
items.summary: Chinese suppliers have refused to ship yttrium, terbium, gallium and indium-phosphide to US buyers since early August after Beijing sanctioned the Responsible Business Alliance; Japan recorded near-zero terbium exports and a 98% yttrium drop (Jan-Aug) versus a year earlier. China still controls roughly 99% of heavy rare-earth processing, so near-term diversification isn't realistic before the summit.
items.actionable: The squeeze is real and ongoing, not just rhetoric -- treat any pre-summit goodwill gesture from Beijing as tactical, not structural, so the ex-China rare-earth watchlist thesis stays intact through a possible short-term relief rally.

items.headline: USA Rare Earth breaks ground on $1.2B South Carolina magnet complex
items.summary: USAR broke ground on an 800,000-sq-ft facility in Blacksburg, SC (124 acres, ~490 jobs), targeting 6,400 metric tons/year of sintered NdFeB magnets plus 5,000 tons of strip-cast metal/alloy, complementing its existing Oklahoma plant. Commissioning is targeted for 2028.
items.actionable: A long-lead-time capacity story, not an immediate price catalyst, but it reinforces the US-onshoring thesis behind the rare-earth watchlist independent of this week's summit headlines.

items.headline: MP Materials short interest at 20.4% of float as rare-earth curbs rally the stock
items.summary: MP Materials shares have rallied on China's rare-earth export curbs, with 18 analysts averaging a Strong Buy rating and a 12-month price target of $75.38 (about +49% from Friday's $50.51 close); short interest sits at 20.4% of MP's available float.
items.actionable: High short interest means any friendly summit headline (or an actual export resumption) could trigger an outsized squeeze -- worth sizing the watchlist entry with that asymmetry in mind.

items.headline: Gold and silver whipsaw through the CPI print; Sunday's futures reopen extends the resilience
items.summary: Gold opened Friday at its lowest level in over a month ahead of CPI, then reversed to close near $4,385-4,389/oz; silver swung between a 2.6% intraday loss and a recovery toward $65. Sunday's electronic reopen extended the resilience -- gold futures +0.25% to $4,377.30, silver futures roughly flat at $64.54 -- with metals shrugging off both a near-90%-priced hike and the Hormuz-signing postponement.
items.actionable: Avoid adding leverage to the miners sleeve until Wednesday's FOMC outcome is confirmed -- the two-sided whipsaw through both CPI and the weekend's geopolitical news shows genuine risk in either direction.

items.headline: S&P snaps four-day losing streak (+0.86% to 7,657) as VIX collapses ~11-12%
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose to roughly 7,657, ending four straight down sessions, while the VIX fell about 11-12% to near 15.6-15.8 as easing volatility outweighed the hotter-than-expected core CPI. Weekly breadth was narrower than the index move -- Nasdaq new lows (128) badly outnumbered new highs (38) over the week even as Friday's NYSE advancers/decliners ran roughly 2:1 bullish.
items.actionable: The vol collapse is a genuine short-term relief signal sitting on eroding weekly breadth -- use the calm to review hedges on the large cash pile rather than chasing the rally into a live FOMC decision.

items.headline: Silver on track for a sixth straight annual supply deficit; 2026 gap projected near 67 million ounces
items.summary: The silver market is heading for its sixth consecutive year where industrial and investment demand outstrips mine-plus-recycled supply, with the 2026 shortfall projected around 67 million ounces against total supply near 1.05 billion ounces. Mine output fell about 2% in 2026 despite record-high prices because roughly 70% of mined silver is a byproduct of lead/zinc/copper operations.
items.actionable: The structural deficit underpins the long-term case for the silver-miners sleeve independent of this week's Fed-driven volatility -- a reason to hold through the CPI/FOMC noise rather than trade around it.

items.headline: Tencent's Hunyuan Hy4 tops OpenRouter usage; Tencent flags rivals' AI-model distillation
items.summary: Tencent's open-source Hunyuan Hy4 reportedly became the most-used model on OpenRouter. Separately, Tencent said it detected and disrupted illicit model-distillation activity by Alibaba, Moonshot, DeepSeek, Xiaomi and Zhipu across roughly 190 million exchanges, part of a broader industry advisory context.
items.actionable: Modestly supportive for Tencent's AI positioning narrative; watch for any reputational spillover to Xiaomi given it's named among the flagged distillers.

items.headline: Singapore's REIT sector down 8.2% YTD versus the STI's +24.6% as the market re-prices Fed hikes
items.summary: The FTSE ST All-Share REIT Index is down 8.2% year-to-date as of early September, badly lagging the Straits Times Index's 24.6% gain, as investors shift from pricing Fed cuts to pricing hikes. Analysts still hold an overweight-but-selective stance on S-REITs, favoring names with fixed-rate debt and defensive earnings.
items.actionable: With a Fed hike now ~85-90% priced for Wednesday, expect continued pressure on Keppel REIT/Mapletree PACT-type names until the FOMC outcome is confirmed -- stay selective/defensive rather than adding on dips this week.
